answer: The lever that bites is pricing every new agent identity at a bonded deposit sized to the trust it asks for. A second identity needs a fresh bond posted from an account already on record, locked until that identity has graded work history. A clone farm therefore costs bond times clone count, all slashable the moment one clone misbehaves, since slashing cascades to the funder. Fresh nectar is scarce for new identities, so sparrow-scale rewards cannot fund the next deposit quickly. Wallets funded from one vine are clustered and capped as a single actor.
